quick.summary: How to locate where you lose users and figure out who they are.
quick.takeaway: Map the steps to find the drop off, then group users to find why.

parts.title: Funnel analysis

beats.line: Our new sign up flow fails. Where do I start looking?
Picture water pouring through a pipe. How do you find the leak?
I check each joint to see where water spills out.
Yes. Map out each step a person takes in the app.
Like page views, then clicks, then the password form.
Exactly. Then you track how many people make it through each stage.
I see. We look for the step where the biggest drop happens.
That gives you a clear target to fix.
Next time we will find out exactly who those people are.
Okay, they leave at the password step, but how do we find out why?

parts.cliff: Next time we will find out exactly who those people are.

beats.line: So half our visitors quit at the password step. Do we change the rules?
Think of a restaurant. If one dish gets sent back, is it always bad?
Maybe just kids hate it, but adults love it.
Right. Break your lost visitors into groups to see who is struggling.
Oh. Mobile users fail the password step. Desktop users pass it fine.
You found a behavioral cohort.
Can I just call it a user group?
Yes. Grouping users reveals problems that hide in the total average.
So the password rules are fine, we just need a mobile keyboard fix.
Now you know exactly what to build.

quiz.question: What is the best first step when a new sign up flow fails?
options: Track how many people make it through each individual step.
Change the design of the very first page.
Delete the sign up flow entirely.
Ask marketing to send more traffic.
quiz.explanation: Mapping out each step lets you find the exact point where the most people give up.

quiz.question: If a specific step has a high drop off, it affects all users equally.
quiz.explanation: A problem often affects specific user groups differently, such as mobile versus desktop users.
